summary:
## Options-Considered structure check
FAIL (auto-reject criterion 1: section absent). Plan uses ranked-candidate table + do-NOT-extract table with real per-item rejection reasons (not throwaway phrases) but never uses literal `## Options Considered` / `### Option N:` H3 format fo

insight: gepa-core lives INSIDE the plugins-common monorepo, so Gate Zero + plugin-std extraction are in-repo; consumer migrations for runner-plugin / dev-team / astramem-plugin are cross-repo and need companion FEATs in those backlogs.

The runner loop CLI statically imports `@astragenie/astramem-client` in `memory-context.mts`, so `memory.enabled=never` does NOT bypass it — the package had to be present in the runner plugin cache `node_modules` or every loop command ENOENTs at slice-start.
plugin-std needed a `tsconfig.build.json` to emit `dist/*.d.ts` before workspace consumers (gepa-core) could typecheck against it.
`PluginError` uses `instanceof` for `isPluginError`/`isTransient` — fragile if plugin-std is ever dual-bundled; fine under workspace symlink today.

Reviewers catch real gaps the builder's own green run misses: `rotate()`'s primary size>maxBytes branch had zero coverage despite all tests passing. Frozen-for-migration APIs need branch coverage, not just happy-path — added via test-automator top-up (13→15 tests).

Builder mid-edit IDE diagnostics (syntax error, Promise-used-as-iterable) were transient — resolved by the builder's own self-verify before return; independent re-typecheck confirmed. Do NOT edit files a builder is actively touching on the strength of mid-flight diagnostics.

`readSafe` torn-line counting is position-agnostic (mid-file corruption counted same as torn final line, no line number) — acceptable now, flagged for a diagnostics follow-up since the module is shared/frozen.

The correctness reviewer caught a real resource leak (shared-AbortSignal listener accumulation in `withTimeoutSignal`) that BOTH the builder's green run and the parallel TS reviewer missed — it was pre-existing in gepa-core's original `linkSignal` but the extraction centralized + broadened it to gemini/ollama. Adversarial "does it leak under a shared signal?" review beats happy-path suites for shared/frozen utils.

Fixing the leak before freezing the API (rather than deferring) was the right call: gepa-core's sequential-runner passes ONE signal across a whole GEPA run — the leak would grow with judge-call count in exactly the long-loop workload this package serves.
Consistency matters on a frozen surface: http.ts initially exposed only via `./http` subpath while jsonl.ts was dual-exposed (root + subpath). Aligned to root re-export.

Pure-extraction slices (no in-repo consumer) still get full value from a hard test matrix: the CRLF/LF/BOM deep-equality matrix + round-trip fidelity tests are what make a frozen API safe for the cross-repo consumers that WILL adopt it, standing in for a first-consumer proof this repo can't provide.

`parseFrontmatter<T>` casts unvalidated YAML straight to the caller's generic — acceptable ONLY because the module's documented scope is "no domain validation, caller owns it". If a future consumer wants validated parsing, that's a separate zod-boundary helper, not a change to this core.
First new third-party runtime dep of the milestone (`yaml@^2.6.0`) — no YAML parser existed in the workspace to reuse. Single-entry, no transitive bloat, resolved 2.9.0.

The correctness reviewer's empirical probing (running real execFile against this machine) caught a HIGH the builder's green suite missed: `maxBuffer` overflow (Node default 1MB, trips on verbose `git log`/`diff`) was misclassified as a spawn failure and thrown as a WRONG-category `TransientError`. The initial two-way (exit-code vs spawn-failure) discrimination was too coarse — child_process has a THIRD failure mode (ran-but-output-too-big) that is deterministic, not transient.

Error-category correctness matters as much as pass/fail: a retryable-vs-deterministic misclassification on a frozen API would mislead every downstream consumer's retry logic. Fixed to `DeterministicError`/`E_GIT_MAXBUFFER` before freeze.

Timeout tests need a deterministic race: the builder's first timeout test used `git --version` (too fast, racy) — switched to `git hash-object --stdin` (blocks on stdin EOF that never comes) so a 1ms timeout reliably wins. "Assert it settles" is not a real assertion; assert the concrete outcome (`ok:false`/`status:-1` via SIGTERM).

A builder PASS claim ("typecheck exit 0") is not evidence — live LSP diagnostics showed 8 type errors in file-lock-manager.ts. Re-running the actual command showed exit 0 (diagnostics were a stale mid-edit snapshot). Lesson: verify with a fresh command run; treat both the builder claim AND the IDE diagnostic as untrusted until reproduced.

The "inconsistency" framed by FEAT-008 hid a real design tension between two accepted decisions (DEC-001 never-throws-acquire vs result.ts throw-for-infra). Resolved by recognizing lock contention is a domain outcome (ok(null)), not infra — so throw-for-infra and never-throws-on-contention are not in conflict. Not a mechanical sweep.

The adversarial correctness reviewer paid for itself: it reproduced a live path-traversal exploit (`--plugin ../../evil` wrote agents.json OUTSIDE outputDir + stamped the raw traversal string as `sourcePlugin`) that the builder's 38 green tests + the TS-idiom reviewer both missed. Green tests prove the happy path; only an adversarial "try to break the security boundary" pass finds the injection. For any slice that builds a value-flows-to-filesystem/CI boundary, a dedicated security review is non-optional.

Sanitize EVERY externally-controlled value that reaches a path or a published manifest, not just the obvious one. The builder validated frontmatter `name` (AC-5) but missed `opts.plugin` (the CLI arg used for BOTH path construction and `sourcePlugin` stamping) and `version`. One unguarded input undid the whole allow-list.

Stale IDE diagnostics fired 3× this slice (missing node/bun libs, unused renameSync) contradicting a clean `tsc --noEmit`; each was a mid-edit LSP snapshot, not a real error. Re-running the actual command is the only trustworthy signal.

AC-3 staleness is a DOMAIN outcome, not an error — the reader warns (`stale_registry`) and still resolves `found:true`; a stale entry that stopped resolving would be a different, equally-wrong failure. The builder correctly kept resolveName throw-free (not-found/stale/uncomparable all Result-shaped) per DEC-002, and the tests assert the stale entry STILL resolves, which is the subtle correctness point.

Version comparison is exactly the place NOT to hand-roll: builder added the `semver` package (vs the deliberate no-ajv hand-roll for schema) because prerelease/build-metadata parsing is error-prone — right call, different from the SLICE-1 validator decision.

product_completeness scored 0.78 (not higher) because the slice met the FEAT's AC-3 but under-delivered vs the ADR's broader reader description (multi-producer merge + cross-plugin collision detection) with no descope note in the plan — see Followups.

A pre-work architect ADR earns its keep when it is CONSUMED: this ADR's five decisions (push-not-pull, producer-semver versioning, semver.lt staleness comparator, per-producer file-pair layout, throw-DeterministicError failures) were each directly implemented by SLICE-1 and SLICE-3 without rework — the design held under build. That's the signal a pre-flight ADR was worth the 3 points.

The architect corrected a false premise in the FEAT itself: the stated precedent (@astragenie/astramem-client) is a hand-written published client, NOT a generated manifest — only pinned-artifact-consumption transfers. Catching that before build stopped SLICE-1 from copying an inapplicable pattern.
